source.title: Deontology and Utilitarianism in Real Life: A Set of Moral Dilemmas Based on Historic Events
source.changes: De-identified and reworded; incidental details generalised; question in yes/no form.

kept: You are the twins’ parent with your partner; the two girls share organs.
The weaker girl’s brain activity is reduced and her vital organs function poorly; the stronger girl’s separate organs are normal and currently support both.
Growth will make this double strain unsustainable after a few months.
Without surgery doctors say both soon die; surgery kills the weaker girl and gives the stronger a very good survival chance and a possibly largely unimpaired life.
Doctors perform the operation you authorise; the children, rather than you, receive the stated survival benefit, and the sacrificed child is among the two otherwise threatened.
The suggested action is to have the girls separated with shared organs given to the stronger girl.
rewrite: You and your partner became parents a few weeks ago to two girls joined at birth. They share some organs. The weaker baby has reduced brain activity and poorly functioning vital organs. All the stronger baby’s separate organs developed normally. Doctors explain that the stronger girl’s organs currently sustain the weaker one, but after a few months of growth they will no longer bear the strain of supporting both. They propose separating the girls and assigning the shared organs to the stronger baby. According to the doctors, both girls will soon die without surgery. With surgery, the weaker baby will die during the procedure. The stronger baby has a very good chance of surviving and might live a largely unimpaired life. Do you let your twins be separated?
notes: Deliberately retained: two joined girls, one sustaining the other, and the shared-organ allocation; these determine the one-versus-two survival choice and victim-beneficiary overlap. Anatomical generalisation may change perceived medical realism.

generalised.why: the particular shared organ does not change the dependency
